notes: Gemini API paid-tier standard rates, USD per 1M tokens, read 2026-10-13 from the pricing page HTML. gemini-4-argon: INTRODUCTORY $2.00 input / $0.10 cached input / $10.00 output (output includes thinking tokens) 'through November 30, 2026'; STANDARD $4.00 / $0.20 / $20.00 'starting December 1, 2026'. The row carries valid_from 2026-10-13, valid_until 2026-11-30 and the standard rate in post_valid_until, the same shape as the gemini-3.8-flash promo row in google-api-2026-07.json. Google's launch post footnote words the end condition as 'After the introductory period expires on November 30, 2026, the price of $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens will apply. Applies to the Argon model intended for public access only.' Cache: Argon supports implicit caching only; explicit caching (cachedContents) is not supported. The developer guide says cached input is discounted 95% on hits (to $0.10, then $0.20), implicit caching is on by default for prompts of at least 4,096 tokens on the Gemini API (the Vertex page says 6,144). No cache write fee and no cache storage fee is listed for Argon, so cache_write_per_m is 0 and means none published (explicit-cache storage does not apply). Long context: the Argon section of the pricing page lists a single rate set and no >200k-token tier; the Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview section on the same page does list one (input $2.00 for prompts up to 200k tokens, $4.00 above), so the absence for Argon is meaningful but is the absence of a published tier, not a statement that none exists. The 1,048,576-token window is shared across input, thinking and output. Other service classes on the same page, recorded here because the schema has no field for them (per 1M tokens, intro then standard): Batch $1.00 / $5.00 / $0.05 then $2.00 / $10.00 / $0.10; Flex the same as Batch; Priority $3.60 / $18.00 / $0.18 then $7.20 / $36.00 / $0.36. Search and Maps grounding: 5,000 free requests per month shared across Gemini 3 and newer models, then $14 per 1,000. Argon is not available on the Free tier or on the Google AI Pro plan. Vertex / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (separate price list, source google-agent-platform-pricing-2026-10-13): Standard global $2 / $0.1 / $10 through 2026-11-30 then $4 / $0.2 / $20; non-global endpoints are 10% higher ($2.2 / $0.11 / $11 then $4.4 / $0.22 / $22). The Vertex page footnotes the intro price as 'promotional pricing provided through 50% credits back on net spend on select models', which does not apply to gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive; its standard rate is $4 / $0.2 / $20 from the start. MATCHING: the pattern list has one entry, gemini-4-argon, on purpose. A bare gemini-4 pattern would price any later Gemini 4 sibling (Google says more Gemini 4 models are coming) at Argon rates. gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive (Vertex-only, allowlist-only, Fairwind Program) contains the substring gemini-4-argon, so first-substring matching WOULD price it at the Argon intro rate, which Google says does not apply to it; it is not catalogued, so consumers that can see that id should treat it as unpriced here. WARNING for consumers that load only google-api-2026-07.json (for example the tokensmash vendored copy, whose list in scripts/sync_tokensmash_pricing.sh names only that Google file): that file ends with a family_default pattern 'gemini' that maps to gemini-3.1-pro-preview ($2.00 / $12.00), so gemini-4-argon resolves to the wrong model and the wrong output price ($12 vs $10 intro, $12 vs $20 standard) there. This file must be loaded as well, ahead of the 2026-07 file's fallback, or the sync script list must be extended. Artificial Analysis lists Argon at the intro rates (see performance files). Recheck on 2026-11-30 (intro end; the valid_until row then expires and the validator will flag it until the row is updated to the standard rate) and on any Google price change. Roster note: gemini-3.7-flash and gemini-3.5-flash were deprecated 2026-10-08 (changelog) and are auto-routed to 3.8-flash and 3.6-flash; their rows in google-api-2026-07.json are unchanged. Other Gemini rows were not re-verified in this file; the 2026-10-07 re-verification in google-api-2026-07.json is the latest full read.
